postings.title: Software Engineer
postings.text:
Software Engineer
South San Francisco, CA
Engineering
Full-Time
Apply for this job
http://www.emeraldcloudlab.com
About Emerald
At Emerald, we are building the software and hardware infrastructure to accelerate the pace of life sciences research, laying the foundations for an era of flourishing biotechnology innovation in the coming decades. It is our aim to make it as straightforward for a determined scientist to bring into reality an ambitious new idea for a cure as it has become for a capable programmer to start a web-based software company.
The Emerald Cloud Laboratory (ECL) is a web-based life sciences lab. It empowers scientists to specify experiments with the precision and reproducibility of code, and to abstract away the physical execution of those experiments to Emerald’s robotically-driven facility. Through the ECL, the resulting experimental data is accessible in perpetuity, detailed metadata is linked and explorable, and investigators are equipped with a suite of computational tools to take care of the algorithmic aspects of data analysis, freeing them to focus on the insights that are uniquely derived by scientists.
Emerald Engineering
Build the software foundations of 21st century biotech
As a member of Emerald Engineering, you will be one of the earliest individuals on the team, and will have significant ownership over the software direction. We’re a small team setting the course for how the lab jumps into the cloud, and your versatility as an engineer, both in terms of movement up and down the stack and in terms of raw creativity, will be consistently stretched.
You will be creating the products and infrastructure that enable scientists to move from manual benchwork back to what they do best: namely, science. This entails full stack web development on the ECL product used by our customers and our internal Research Team, as well as growing the core software infrastructure on which our Scientific Development Team relies to translate the lab into code.
The engineering culture at Emerald is at the heart of what makes us different among biotechs. It underlies our aggressive robotic automation of lab processes, along with the focus we apply in our internal research to reproducibility, tooling, and modularity. Every scientist we hire learns to code, we track our lab notebooks in git, and a “day in the life” for a scientist at Emerald looks suspiciously similar to that of a software engineer. There is still so much room for this culture to grow, and it will primarily be the early members of our Engineering team who are entrusted to amplify it.
About You
We’re looking for strong generalists, with bonus points if your experience slants toward deep front-end expertise
You might be a great fit for Emerald Engineering if …
- You’re an expert in a core web programming language like Python, JavaScript, Ruby, or Go. Being an expert means not only deep familiarity with the language but also the open source frameworks and libraries that make you love it. We’re Go and JavaScript/CoffeeScript, so big bonus points if you love them too, but we strongly believe that good coders are good in any language, so if that’s you we want to hear from you.
- You are engaged with the myriad of technologies available today that allow three smart engineers to do what would have required 15 a few years ago. On our list for these kinds of tech: AWS, Github, CI, Docker.
- You have worked extensively with a cloud provider such as AWS.
- If you consider yourself more of a “front-end” developer, you have expertise in some JavaScript framework like Angular, Ember, etc.
- You are pragmatic about engineering practice and ways to optimize it. This means you know why Github is more than just a VCS, and you believe that untested code is unfinished code.
- You have experience / interest in functional programming. It's especially auspicious if you've worked with Mathematica.
You might be a great fit for Emerald's culture if …
- You’ve got grit. Setbacks just sweeten the eventual wins.
- You regard your work as a craft you are on a long road to honing, and you insist on keeping a codebase that is a pleasure to work in.
- When a hard problem confronts you, you are too busy conceiving of potential solutions to get hung up on the question of whether it can be solved or not.
- You are impressively empathetic. Being a good teammate means pushing clear code, and at Emerald, being a “product-focused engineer” includes thinking like a scientist.
- You are curious and excited to work hand-in-hand with scientists, and to learn their domains.
- You are not afraid to diverge from precedent when first-principles thinking illuminates another path.
Next Steps
If you would like to apply or learn more, we’d love to hear from you! Please follow the "Apply" link below, and include your resume and a remark or two about where you are coming from and why you are interested in Emerald and this role. We will contact you if we think there could be a match.
Optional but welcome:
A link to your Github account is great. We find links to any projects you are proud of to be especially helpful. With project links, please include some explanation to help us get our bearings.

postings.title: Laboratory Operator I
postings.text:
The Laboratory Operations (Lab Ops) team is charged with executing the logistical aspects of our laboratory processes. All scientifically relevant aspects of each experiment are executed using robotics and automation, and it is the job of Lab Ops to setup and maintain the robotic instrumentation on which the entire lab runs. The experiments span many disciplines, including organic chemistry, analytical chemistry, physical chemistry, molecular biology and cell biology. Laboratory Operators gain experience in this expansive diversity of experiments and with our cutting-edge hardware and software.
As a Laboratory Operator I, you will run essential maintenance protocols for the instruments and the laboratory. These protocols are critical to sustaining the high quality operation of the facilities and provide experience working in ECL’s unique, systematic lab environment with our integrated software tools. An ideal candidate will be excited to contribute to the objective of Lab Ops team as a whole in order to make the cloud lab a reality, will appreciate the importance of this work and will take pride in completing it with exceptional quality.
About You
We’re seeking relentless, detail-oriented individuals to drive the extremely fast turnaround of experiments conducted through the ECL, and uphold the quality of all laboratory processes.
About ECL
www.emeraldcloudlab.com
The Emerald Cloud Laboratory (ECL) enables life scientists to move out of the lab, and to conduct research entirely from a computer. Stepping away from manual completion of experiments at the bench, scientists on the ECL leverage the remote, automated execution of all standard biology and chemistry experiments in Emerald’s industrial lab facilities, working within a software platform for all stages of research workflows, from experimental design to data analysis.

postings.title: Application Software Engineer
postings.text:
The Application Software Engineer develops the ECL Command Center and the multiple internal applications on which the ECL runs. The Command Center is a desktop application built with web technologies. It offers scientists a broad suite of tools for designing experiments on the ECL, tracking their progress, and analyzing their results, all within the collaborative context of working alongside other researchers. Projects include: the notebook interface to Emerald’s Symbolic Lab Language (SLL); team-based features for managing projects and end-to-end research workflows; point-and-click command builders that onboard users into the capabilities of SLL; building out the platform for running the web application on the desktop.
We’re a small team, which means it is essential for every team member to be ready to take ownership and lead projects. Feature development and proximity to overall UX are both central in this role, so the Application Software Engineer works very closely alongside the outstanding ECL Design team.
As an early team member helping to build the Engineering team as well as the product, you will also be encouraged to contribute to the software engineering practices we maintain in our own work, and which we bring to ECL as a whole. We strive to be continually critical of our process, cutting cruft and homing in on performance multipliers (such as continuous integration and agile development practices).
Our Tech Stack
Our applications are web apps (React / HTML5 / CSS3) running on the desktop using NW.js, across Windows and Mac OS. Our backend services are written in Go, and deployed on AWS infrastructure in Docker containers, with container orchestration through Kubernetes. Our source code control is on Github, with integration with Travis CI for continuous testing. The Symbolic Lab Language is written in the Wolfram Language. Our stack is always evolving, and we welcome new ideas and technologies which enhance our ability to deliver incredible software.
The Application Engineering role operates primarily in frontend technologies like React and Redux. More broadly, developing the software to enable cloud-based science is an expansive, diverse challenge. A core component of our job is consistently determining the right tools for the job at hand, and diving in to learn these new technologies along the way.

postings.title: Scientific Computing Engineer
postings.text:
The charge of the Scientific Computing team at ECL is to build into Emerald's Symbolic Lab Language (SLL) a broad suite of analysis and simulation functions to accompany the comprehensive array of experimental capabilities running on the instrumentation in ECL facilities. These experimental techniques range across fields as diverse as physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, organic chemistry, molecular biology and cell biology.
The analysis and simulation functions in SLL serve as the computational tools necessary to drive the experimental design and data analysis steps in research workflows alongside the SLL experiment functions which directly control the conduct of those experiments in the lab. Developing these tools entails incorporating existing models and algorithms along with developing novel representations and models, and building the higher level capabilities these enable in analysis and simulation.

postings.title: Scientific Developer
postings.text:
The Scientific Developer at ECL exemplifies the ideal of the "Engineering-driven Scientist". Every scientist at Emerald learns to code, working in the Wolfram Language, and the eclectic team comes together to tackle the singular challenges at the intersection of understanding experimental detail, architecting the logistics for a new model of industrial lab facility, integrating new instrumentation, and building the software system that captures it all.
The charge of the Scientific Development team is to build the interface in code to the physical laboratory. This involves prototyping, automating, and codifying scientific experimentation which spans multiple disciplines, including molecular biology, cell biology, organic chemistry, analytical chemistry, and physical chemistry. Working on this team, you will combine existing laboratory and experimental expertise with programming and robotic systems, and you will master an enormous span of scientific and engineering techniques.
On the SciDev team, you will be driving the core development of the ECL, and your work will have a different character than traditional scientific paths. First, ECL is built on an engineering culture. This culture underlies everything from our relentless automation of lab processes to the focus on reproducibility and tools in software that is pervasive in the day-to-day. Second, you will be designing a system and an interface, requiring an eye for consistency and elegance, and invoking your own perspective as a scientific researcher to craft one of the first software systems that scientists everywhere love to use.
About You
We are seeking extremely versatile, engineering-driven scientists who are excited to bring together a seasoned perspective in lab-based science with an inventiveness in software to reshape scientific research.

postings.title: Platform Engineer
postings.text:
The  Emerald Cloud Laboratory  (ECL) enables life scientists to move out of the lab, and to conduct research entirely from a computer. Stepping away from manual completion of experiments at the bench, scientists on the ECL leverage the remote, automated execution of all standard biology and chemistry experiments in Emerald’s industrial lab facilities, working within a software platform for all stages of research workflows, from experimental design to data analysis. Our system empowers scientists at Big Pharma companies, startups, and academic laboratories by allowing them to run wet lab experiments from anywhere in the world without ever stepping foot into the lab.
Engineering at ECL
The Platform Engineer builds the distributed software systems that support the ECL, designing the way in which those systems are safely and scalably deployed in Docker containers on AWS, and contributing to core low-level components of Emerald's Symbolic Lab Language (SLL). Projects include: building a hybrid object / graph multi-tenant data store that supports describing all standard biology and chemistry experiments in code; managing the deployment of Kubernetes, enabling environment parity between our development and production environments; building a service to safely distribute and execute simulation, analysis, and testing code in SLL; working closely with our Scientific Development team in developing and optimizing data storage, retrieval and search functions in SLL. We’re a small team, which means it is essential for every team member to be ready to take ownership and lead projects.
As an early team member helping to build the Engineering team as well as the product, you will also be encouraged to contribute to the software engineering practices we maintain in our own work, and which we bring to ECL as a whole. We strive to be continually critical of our process, cutting cruft and homing in on performance multipliers (such as continuous integration and agile development practices).
Our Tech Stack
Our backend services are written in Go, and deployed on AWS infrastructure in Docker containers, with container orchestration through Kubernetes. Our applications are Electron web apps (React / HTML5 / CSS3) running on the desktop across Windows and Mac OS. Our source code control is on Github, with integration with Travis CI for continuous testing. SLL and the Experiment Framework are written in the Wolfram Language. Our stack is always evolving, and we welcome new ideas and technologies which enhance our ability to deliver incredible software.
The Platform Engineering role operates mostly in Go, AWS (Postgres RDS, S3, EC2, SQS, etc.), Docker, Kubernetes and the Wolfram Language. More broadly, bringing online the first cloud-based biotech lab is an expansive, diverse challenge. A core component of our job is consistently determining the right tools for the job at hand, and diving in to learn these new technologies along the way.
\n
Requirements
- Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science.
- Knowledge of software programming in Java, Python, AWS, Go, Mathematica.

- Creating and modifying entries in the holistic company database of all objects.
- CAD modeling and 3D printing.
- CAM programming and CNC milling.
- Researching and learning new techniques.
- PLM (product lifecycle management) of all components used by the team.
- Learning the skills and techniques required to perform any of the above responsibilities as none of these are prerequisite knowledge.
Required Experience:
- Bachelors with a background in science or engineering discipline.
- Familiarity with daily work and logistics of a laboratory.
- Ability to read and understand technical documentation and drawings.

- Knowledge regarding process improvement tools and techniques.
- Experience with hand and power tool safety use.
- Familiarity with programming languages such as Wolfram Mathematica.
